theory.intro: Recipes, paint and concrete mixes, scale drawings and shared profits all use the same part thinking. Write down the ratio or scale the situation gives, find the value of one part or the multiplier, then answer the question in a sensible unit.
facts: A scale is written **image : original**, so $1:n$ means $1$ unit on the drawing is $n$ units in real life.
Drawing to real life: **multiply** by $n$; real life to drawing: **divide** by $n$.
Do the scaling first and convert the units afterwards, e.g. $6\times50\,000=300\,000$ cm $=3$ km.
To scale a recipe, find the multiplier $\text{new}\div\text{old}$ and apply it to **every** ingredient.
When something is shared in the same ratio as contributions, simplify the contributions to a ratio first.
steps: Write down the ratio or scale the situation gives
Find the value of $1$ part, or the multiplier
Scale up or down to answer the question, using a sensible unit

foundation.question_text: A map has a scale of $1:50\,000$. Two towns are $6$ cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life, in kilometres?
foundation.solution_text:
$6\times50\,000=300\,000\text{ cm}$
$300\,000\div100=3000\text{ m}$
$3000\div1000=3\text{ km}$
The towns are $3$ km apart.

foundation.question_text: A model city is built to a scale of $1:1000$. A tower is $240$ m tall in real life. How tall is the model of the tower, in centimetres?
foundation.solution_text:
$240\div1000=0.24\text{ m}$
$0.24\times100=24\text{ cm}$
The model tower is $24$ cm tall.

foundation.question_text: A pancake recipe for $4$ people uses $200$ g of flour, $300$ mL of milk and $2$ eggs. How much of each ingredient is needed for $10$ people?

Ana invests $\$8000$ and Raj invests $\$12\,000$ to start a business. They agree to share the profit in the same ratio as their investments. How much of a $\$45\,000$ profit does each of them receive?
Three cousins share $\$360$. Ola takes $\$90$ and the rest is shared between Kit and Mo in the ratio $2:7$. How much does Mo receive?

development.question_text: A bushwalking map has a scale of $1:125\,000$. On the map, the distance between the ranger station and the bee farm is $45$ mm. What is the real-life distance between them, in kilometres?
A map has a scale of $1:500\,000$. Two cities are $75$ km apart in real life. How far apart are they on the map, in centimetres?
development.solution_text:
$75\text{ km}=75\,000\text{ m}=7\,500\,000\text{ cm}$
$7\,500\,000\div500\,000=15\text{ cm}$
They are $15$ cm apart on the map.

development.question_text: A muffin recipe makes $6$ muffins from $150$ g of flour, $90$ g of sugar and $60$ g of butter. Sam has exactly $250$ g of flour and plenty of everything else. What is the greatest number of whole muffins he can make, and how much sugar will he need for them?
development.solution_text:
$150\div6=25\text{ g of flour per muffin}$
$250\div25=10\text{ muffins}$
$90\div6=15\text{ g of sugar per muffin}$
$15\times10=150\text{ g}$
He can make $10$ muffins, needing $150$ g of sugar.

development.question_text: Mortar is made from cement and sand in the ratio $1:5$. A builder has $4$ kg of cement and $25$ kg of sand. Which material runs out first, and how much mortar can be made?
development.solution_text:
$1\text{ part}=4\text{ kg of cement}$
$5\text{ parts}=20\text{ kg of sand}$
$25-20=5\text{ kg of sand left over}$
$4+20=24\text{ kg}$
The cement runs out first, and $24$ kg of mortar can be made.

development.question_text: Sam, Eddie and Maria invested $\$1500$, $\$5000$ and $\$9500$ respectively when they started a business. An annual profit of $\$480\,000$ is shared in the same ratio as their investments. How much does each of them receive?
Adam, Bertie and Cameron share $\$240$. Cameron receives $20\%$ more money than Adam, and the ratio of Adam's share to Bertie's share is $5:1$. How much does each of them receive?
development.solution_text:
$A:B=5:1$
$C=1.2\times5=6\text{ parts}$
$A:B:C=5:1:6$
$12\text{ parts}=\$240$
$1\text{ part}=\$20$
$5\text{ parts}=\$100$
$6\text{ parts}=\$120$
Adam receives $\$100$, Bertie $\$20$ and Cameron $\$120$.

mastery.question_text: A map maker wants to draw a map of an area measuring $8$ km by $8$ km, and decides to use a scale of $1:100$. Explain why this scale is not appropriate.
mastery.solution_text:
$8\text{ km}=800\,000\text{ cm}$
$800\,000\div100=8000\text{ cm}=80\text{ m}$
The map would be $80$ m by $80$ m, which is far too large to print or carry, so the scale is not appropriate.

mastery.question_text: A $24$ kg bag of dry concrete mix contains cement, sand and gravel in the ratio $1:2:3$. A builder empties the whole bag into a mixer, but the job needs a mix in the ratio $1:2:4$. How much extra gravel must he add?
mastery.solution_text:
$6\text{ parts}=24\text{ kg}$
$1\text{ part}=4\text{ kg}$
$1:2:3=4:8:12\text{ kg}$
The cement stays at $4$ kg, so $1\text{ part}=4$ kg in the new mix as well.
$4\times4=16\text{ kg of gravel needed}$
$16-12=4\text{ kg}$
He must add $4$ kg of gravel.
